themes.name: AI compute: NVIDIA's supply chain
themes.what: Microsoft ended its deal to anchor Nscale's Loughton, Essex AI site, where it was to rent about 23,000 Nvidia chips, because grid power was not expected until the 2030s (Telegraph, confirmed by Reuters and Bloomberg Oct 18). Debt for Oracle's Michigan campus has fallen to about 87 cents on the dollar from par in July, and Oracle's 5 year default swaps are near a record 300 basis points. Lenders and power, not chip demand, are now the limits.
themes.for_you: No chip swings and no puts on ORCL (128.23, Wait, downtrend) or CRWV (61.39). NVDA (214.13) and MSFT are left out of both lists: Microsoft moved the demand elsewhere rather than cutting it. Watch Meta's capex guide Oct 21.

themes.name: AI power and the grid
themes.what: NiSource signed a 20 year deal on Oct 16 to supply about 1,100 MW to Microsoft's Indiana data center campus from 2028, with Microsoft paying for the generation and transmission and a 600 MW battery deal alongside. Two days later Microsoft walked away from Nscale's UK site because grid power was not expected until the 2030s. Power is now the gate for AI sites.
themes.for_you: No action. NI has no dashboard verdict yet. MSFT (529.05) stays 'Buy zone now'; the deal shows it pays for sites that have power. Utilities with signed hyperscaler contracts (NI, DTE, WEC) are the steadier way to own this than borrowed money builders.

innovations.name: Defense and Security
innovations.what: Rechecked on the daily rotation. Drone Dominance Gauntlet II orders have started (Neros 14,000 drones for over $100 million, Swarm Defense 4,000 for at least $25 million), the Army now expects its first LOCUST X3 laser by Q4 FY2027 and combat use by early 2028, and the Senate leader signaled no new Golden Dome reconciliation money before the midterms. No stage moves: orders are small next to the 60,000 drone plan.
innovations.for_you: No action. AVAV (121.79) is rated Avoid and KTOS (40.42) and RCAT (4.72) Wait: the drone money is real, but most orders go to private makers. LMT (552.09) is 'Buy zone, wait for the chart'; Golden Dome money waiting until after the midterms is a slow drag, not a reason to sell.

countries.name: Brazil
countries.what: AtlasIntel (reported Oct 19) has Flavio Bolsonaro at 49.8% to Lula's 47.6%, or 51.1% to 48.9% of valid votes, down from a 5.4 point lead on Oct 9; Nexus for BTG Pactual has 46.5% to 45.9%. Prediction markets still give Bolsonaro about 77% (Polymarket) to 80% (Kalshi), so polls are tighter than prices.
countries.for_you: No action until after Oct 25. NU (14.56) is 'Buy zone now' (zone 14.03 to 15.08), but a Lula win could hit Brazilian banks hard in a day. All four are left out of both lists while the race is this close.

countries.name: China
countries.what: China's Q3 GDP grew 4.5% from a year ago and 1.2% from Q2, above the 4.4% and 1.0% forecasts; growth for the first nine months is 4.6%, inside the 4.5% to 5% target. Factories carried it: September output rose 5.5%, while retail sales rose only about 1.1% and fixed asset investment fell 7.2% for January to September. The statistics bureau said weak domestic demand 'remains prominent', and analysts see less reason for big Q4 stimulus.
countries.for_you: No action. BABA (109.11) and PDD (80.97) are in downtrends with up/down volume under 0.9, and weak shoppers do not help. FCX and SCCO are left out of both lists: factory output is fine, but less stimulus removes a tailwind.

countries.name: European Union
countries.what: French bonds and stocks fell Oct 19 after a weekend of riots: the 10 year yield rose to about 4.84% to 4.89%, the gap over German bonds reached about 142 to 146 basis points, and the CAC 40 fell about 1% to 1.4% by midday, with Societe Generale and BNP Paribas down more than 2%. Parliament votes on 2027 budget revenues Oct 20 and Moody's reviews France Oct 23. Separately, Trump waived the Graham Act's new Russia tariffs and sanctions on Oct 16, which pushed Brent down about 2% Monday.
countries.for_you: No action. No dashboard name is French. SAN (13.30) and ING (33.45) had up/down volume under 0.75 on Friday, and French stress tends to spill into all euro banks, so do not buy them into Moody's. TTE is left out: cheaper oil and a weaker euro pull in opposite directions.

countries.name: India
countries.what: On Oct 16 Trump waived the Graham Act's tariffs of up to 100% on the top five buyers of Russian crude, two days before they took effect. India is one of the largest buyers, so the threat of a new US tariff on top of the 10% Section 301 rate is gone for now, and Brent fell about 2% to $107.60 on Oct 19, which helps an oil importer.
countries.for_you: No action. INDA (47.66) is still in a downtrend with up/down volume 0.69, so a better headline is not a buy signal yet. HDB and IBN are left out: lower oil helps, but rates are still rising.

countries.name: Japan
countries.what: The Nikkei fell 0.6% to 64,916.70 on Oct 19 (AP) as tech stocks caught up with Friday's US chip losses; it had been down more than 2% earlier in the session (Newsquawk).
countries.for_you: No action. The chip test names stay out of both lists until US chip stocks stop falling. The BOJ meets Oct 30.

countries.name: South Korea
countries.what: The KOSPI rose 1.8% to 5,768.01 on Oct 19 (AP) after the worst week for Samsung and SK hynix since 2008; it is still down more than 17% in a month. Foreign investors sold about 11.2 trillion won ($7.8 billion) of KOSPI stocks last week, and foreign ownership of Samsung fell to 45.98% on Oct 16, the lowest since July 2009 (Seoul Economic Daily).
countries.for_you: No action. One up day after a 14% weekly drop is a bounce. EWY (150.44) had up/down volume 0.93 on Friday. Korean bank ADRs stay hurt into Thursday's rate decision.

countries.name: Taiwan
countries.what: The Taiex fell 0.6%, or 289 points, to 46,822 on Oct 19 after the Philadelphia chip index dropped 3.8% on Friday; TSMC closed flat at NT$2,420 (Focus Taiwan via Ad-hoc News).
countries.for_you: No action. TSM (412.61 Friday) holding flat while the index fell is a small sign of relative strength, but it has no buy zone verdict. EWT (106.26) had up/down volume 0.79 on Friday, so sellers still lead.
